requirements.statement: create, fill, update, save, delete and destroy persist through the bound session with flush only; the caller's commit and rollback decide visibility to other connections; unknown attributes raise KeyError.
all, first, find and find_or_fail keep their results; find returns None and find_or_fail raises ModelNotFoundError for a missing primary key.
with_, with_joined and with_subquery accept string paths, dotted nested string paths, class attributes and nested schema tuples, and loaded relations cause no additional SQL when accessed.

where, sort and smart_query keep Django-like relation filters, operators, descending sort, outer joins, nested or_/and_ structures, hybrid attributes and alias-aware filter_expr/order_expr; unknown names raise KeyError.
Relations joined for filtering or sorting are eager loaded without extra SQL, schema-requested loads are honored, and the standalone smart_query works on a lazy=dynamic relationship query.
columns, primary_keys, relations, settable_relations (without viewonly), hybrid_properties, hybrid_methods and settable_attributes keep their names.
ReprMixin output, to_dict with nested, hybrid_attributes and exclude, and TimestampsMixin columns keep their documented values.
The same behavior holds when only SQLAlchemy moves from 1.4.54 to 2.0.38 with the rest of the lock unchanged; only Python modules under sqlalchemy_mixins/ change.
